newsitem.title: UK: Delta climbs as brokers upgrade stock.
newsitem.headline: Delta climbs as brokers upgrade stock.

text.p: Shares in cable and engineering firm Delta Plc climbed on Monday, buoyed by news of a new chief executive and as brokers upgraded their stance on the stock.
Shares rose 26p to 403 1/2 p by 1020 GMT.
UBS and Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull both upgraded Delta to "buy" from "hold", encouraged by the prospect of new management and signs that business is improving after a difficult first half.
"Our stance is based on the prospects for the new chief executive and a new management approach," said Sash Tusa, electricals analyst at UBS.
The company said in its interim statement that chief executive Robert Easton would be stepping down in November, to be replaced by GKN's Jon Scott-Maxwell.
Analysts said that although profit figures had been unimpressive, there were signs for encouragement.
"On closer examination, the underlying profitability for Delta's businesses look very encouraging which will give the chief executive a firm base from which to work," said Tusa.
Delta said pretax profits after exceptionals fell to 11.5 million stg in the first half of 1996 compared with 35.1 million stg for the first half of 1995.
The company said trading conditions had remained difficult during the first six months but the start of the second half had shown an improvement.
Analysts at SGST said benefits resulting from the restructuring of the cables division were bullish for Delta.
"The restructuring is now finished and the full benefits are expected to come through next year," said an analyst at SGST.
